title: Business debt strategy depends on growth ROI
summary: Business debt isn't automatically "high interest" — if reinvested capital returns more than the debt cost, leverage can be wealth-creating.
detailsHtml:
The leverage decision

For business debt, the right comparison isn't "rate vs. expected investment return" — it's "rate vs. marginal return on capital deployed in the business." A 10% business loan funding a marketing campaign that returns 40% on invested capital is wealth-creating, even at a "high" headline rate. A 6% loan funding equipment that returns 4% is wealth-destroying.

The owner-personal-guarantee issue

Most small-business debt requires owner personal guarantees, meaning the business debt is also functionally personal debt. This shifts the calculus — you're not just risking the business if it fails, you're risking your personal assets. Personal guarantees should be reviewed and renegotiated as the business builds credit history.
